newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Northeast spot power firmer on tighter supply.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Northeast spot power firmer on tighter supply.

text.p: Spot bulk electricity prices in the northeastern U.S. ended firmer Tuesday versus Monday's levels amid reduced amount of generation capacity in the region, market sources said.

The region's utilities started taking some of their fossil-fuel units off line last weekend, especially those that use fuel oil or natural gas, because of lackluster weather-related demand, traders said.
"We have some units on reserve shutdown," said a utility trader in the Northeast.
Some market sources noted less spot hydroelectricity from Quebec this week also reduced the supply availability in the region.
For Wednesday, peak, non-firm electricity in the western New York Power Pool (NYPP) was quoted at $17.00-$18.00 a megawatt hour (MWh), a narrower range than $16.00-$18.00 on Monday.
Interruptible power during Wednesday's light load hours in western NYPP was discussed at $14.00-$15.00, higher than Monday's quote of $9.00-$13.00.
Non-firm electricity prices for heavy load hours on Wednesday in eastern NYPP were assessed at $21.00-$22.00, flat from Monday's values for Tuesday.
Wednesday's off-peak power in the eastern half of NYPP was pegged at $14.00-$15.00, unchanged from Monday's levels.
In the New England Power Pool (NEPOOL), non-firm power during peak demand period on Wednesday was quoted at $29.00-$31.00, compared with Monday's $30.00-$34.00 offers.
Wednesday's non-firm, off-peak electricity prices in NEPOOL was discussed at $21.00-$22.00, flat from Monday. Bids for off-peak deliveries on Wednesday were heard as low as $18.00.

Boston Edison Co's was boosting output from its 670 megawatt (MW) Pilgrim nuclear station in Plymouth, Mass.. The plant was shut two weeks ago because of a saltwater leak in a set of heat exchangers in its reactor building.
New York Power Authority's 800 MW Fitzpatrick nuclear generating facility in Scriba, N.Y., continued to operate at reduced capacity amid repairs to one of its feedwater pumps.
